note: The app now shows RECOVERY WEIGHT - the rocket plus its spent motor casing, which is what a parachute actually has to lower, and not the pad weight it was showing you. On a 4 inch design with an M motor that is 3.38 kg against a 5.74 kg pad weight. It needs a motor loaded. On a two-stage rocket it is the sustainer's weight, because the boosters are on the ground by then. And a new Recovery sizing panel recommends a main and a drogue from it: the size you need at a named drag coefficient, then real canopies from the parts catalogue with the descent rate each would give YOUR rocket - filtered to the ones that will actually pack into your airframe, sized against each canopy's own weight, and using the air at your field rather than at sea level.
